source: daily Fleet trend scout email (2026-10-29), themodernwallet.com section: 2 bullets; DataForSEO-validated
interpretedBrief: The scout gave two bullets for themodernwallet.com. First, new Zillow and Thumbtack research puts the typical cost of owning a home on top of the mortgage at $16,566 a year, and readers want a way to compute their own number. Second, the Fed held rates at 3-3/4 to 4 percent on Oct 28 with two dissents for a hike, and the existing rate-hike guide has no word on it. The audience is buyers and owners rerunning affordability math, and savers and borrowers asking what the hold means.

outline: Intro paragraph 1: the answer (typical $16,566 a year, $1,380 a month, two-thirds maintenance) naming the three lines, and what the calculator returns; paragraph 2: worked default example

howItWorks 1 to 2: what the tool takes in and returns, the default case, and the internal-modeling attribution; why maintenance, property taxes and insurance are separate lines and where to find each figure (links: deductions guide)

howItWorks 3 to 4: the growth rule with the five-year and ten-year totals; where the typical misleads, as three worked cases with stated inputs (low-maintenance home, condo with HOA, high-insurance market) and the like-for-like rule that HOA is left out of the comparison to the national typical

howItWorks 5 to 6: what the five-year change means and why the starting figures are not a forecast (30-metro spread $14,187 to $25,111); the optional mortgage line (links: affordability and rent vs buy calculators)
howItWorks 7 to 8: what the tool leaves out and the limits of the source; the takeaway: budget your own three quotes, with the conditions that change it, and who this is not for

FAQ: 8 questions verbatim from the row prompt (annual cost, hidden costs list, monthly maintenance budget, fastest-rising cost, mortgage included, why mine may be lower, five-year growth, what is left out). The calculator template renders plain paragraphs (no headings or tables), so the page uses prose only
newPageBriefs.contributionAndEvidence: Basis calculated. In our internal cost modeling, we ran the engine over seven scenarios (evidence/hidden-cost-of-owning-a-home-calculator/output.json): national typical $16,566 a year / $1,380.50 a month; maintenance reserve $930.92 a month; $3,000 maintenance gives $8,395 a year; $5,000 insurance gives $19,300; condo with $400 HOA gives $11,729; 3% growth over five years totals $87,951. Inputs: the 2026 Zillow and Thumbtack figures from Zillow's own release of 2026-10-22 (fetched 2026-10-29; Fox Business reports the same). Scenarios S2 to S7 are our illustrative cases and are labeled modeled; S4's $5,000 insurance echoes the release's nearly $5,000 a year in Miami. Reviewer replays the engine independently.
newPageBriefs.tablesToolsVisuals: The calculator (inputs: maintenance, property tax, insurance, HOA monthly, optional mortgage and home value, growth percent, years; outputs: monthly and yearly cost, maintenance reserve, multi-year total, share by line, gap to the national typical, optional all-in monthly and percent of value). No table, image or chart: the calculator template renders plain paragraphs, so the three scenarios are written as short worked cases with their inputs stated beside each result.
newPageBriefs.testingAndReview: TESTED format off: financial topic excluded by _experience.md section G; no executed product tests; ordinary format. Attribution uses 'our internal cost modeling' for the calculated findings and names Fox Business and the Zillow/Thumbtack study as the source of the starting figures. Byline and reviewer come from the template; disclaimer at the bottom only; no first-person testing or client claims.
newPageBriefs.takeaway: Treat $1,380 a month as the national typical starting point, then replace it with your own insurance quote, property tax bill and a maintenance reserve and budget the sum. Applies to a buyer comparing a mortgage payment with owning. A newer home or a condo with HOA-paid exteriors can run well below the typical ($8,395 a year in our $3,000-maintenance scenario) and a high-premium metro well above ($19,300 at $5,000 insurance). Condition that changes it: your own quotes.
